murad.name: Murad
murad.origin: Sultan Murad II was the ruler of the Ottoman Empire. He and his armies invade the small country of Wallachia (now part of the modern country of Romania). In 1444 A.D., the king of Wallachia Vlad Dracul and his son Radu and Vlad II went to the Ottoman Empire, where they planned to negotiate for peace. They were ambushed en route by agents of Murad, who held the sons captive, forcing Vlad the Elder to favor Turkey. This eventually led John Hunyadi and Vlad's other advisers to revolt against him, killing him and his son Mircea Dracula. After five years of torture, Radu had died in captivity, but Vlad was able to escape. In 1459 A.D., Vlad had become king of the vampires and lured Murad into a trap. Dracula's female followers took out Murad's men while Dracula killed Murad personally. After feeding upon on Murad, Dracula tossed Murad's lifeless body to his men.

fields.notes: Murad is based on the real life person, of the Ottoman Empire. In real life, Murad II died in 1451 during a military campaign in Eastern Europe. In late 1450, Murad II led a failed siege of the Castle of Kruje, in an effort to defeat his rival Skanderbeg/George Castriot, Lord of Albania. Murad fell ill in the winter of 1450-1451, and had to call of the campaign and be transported back to his capital Edirne (Adrianople). He died in early February, 1451 due to his illness. He was about 47-years-old at the time of death. Murad II was the father of Mehmed II/Mehmed the Conqueror (1432-1481, reigned 1444-1446, 1451-1481). Mehmed is famous for conquering Constantinople (Istanbul) and the last remnants of the Byzantine Empire, uniting much of Anatolia and the Balkans under his control (through a series of conquests), and leading an unsuccessful invasion of the Italian Peninsula (by the time of his death, he had captured a single Italian city: Otranto.) The real-life Mehmed II and Vlad Tepes ("Dracula", son of the Dragon) spend much of their reigns warring against each other. Vlad is thought to have died in combat in late 1476 or early 1477, with some tales reporting that he was killed in a friendly fire incident. Mehmed died after a sudden illness in 1481, with tales of the time suggesting that he was poisoned.

muramasa.name: Muramasa
muramasa.origin: Muramasa was a legendary Demon blacksmith in Japan. During Japan's century of civil war, starting by mid-15th century, Muramasa forged the Black Blade using a portion of his own dark soul. The Blade caused its possessors to be overcome with unquenchable bloodlust. In the middle of the 20th century, Muramasa was sought out by Logan after his wife, Itsu, and he believed her unborn child as well, were killed in Jasmine Falls. Muramasa agreed to make Logan a sword, forged out of his incredible depths of rage and hatred. The process took many years, but the blade was prepared for Logan when he returned to Muramasa's camp after regaining his full memories after M-Day.

murd blurdock.name: Murd Blurdock
murd blurdock.origin: Murd Blurdock was an Echomelian, a reptilian species that normally lacked eyes but could see by way of echolocation. As a child, Murd was struck by radioactive originium, causing him to lose his echolocation and grow two bulbous eyes. With his newfound ability to see, Murd became the vigilante known as Seeing Being, the Sentient Without Self-Preservation. At some point, Murd's identity was revealed, but he managed to convince the public Seeing Being was actually his secret twin brother. Murd worked as a lawyer with his partner Frogurt "Froggy" Frelson, using his seeing ability to read the expressions on a jury's faces. When Rocket Raccoon was arrested and put on trial for theft, Murd and Froggy were appointed as his legal defense. Minutes before the trial was meant to start, Murd noticed a red-clad female Echomelian at the back of the courtroom holding a sai and a sign saying "COME FIGHT NINJAS." Murd suddenly ran after her, much to Froggy's surprise. Later, Murd was hired by Roberto Da Costa of the New Mutants after they were arrested for trespassing in Shi'ar territory. Murd tried to ask the judge for leniency given the New Mutant's extra-cultural background but his request was denied since the Shi'ar doesn't recognize any space that is not part of their empire. The New Mutants were found guilty and remanded into custody, and Murd was subsequently sanctioned for incompetence.

murderer by spider.name: Murderer by Spider
murderer by spider.origin: This criminal was once a scientist, but nobody trusted in his theories about arthropods and so he started earning money by selling electronic devices that controlled spiders to people who planned murders. He first sell his device to a man who wanted the antiques collection of an old hermit named Adlai Schmidt at all costs, and he succeeded. The second time the former scientist sold his little machines was to another man whose aim was his aunt's inheritance; that time, Spider-Man was able to save the old woman's life and he understood there was an electronic device hidden inside her earrings. Meanwhile, the Murderer by Spider learnt that newspapers (expecially the Daily Bugle) blamed Spidey for the murders and he started working, expecting to face him soon. The criminal created a new device that could led the hero to him by interfering with his Spider-Sense and when Spidey arrived he "switched" his sense off, trying then to kill him with his gun, but the wall-crawler was too fast and disarmed him, so the criminal hid behind a door on which he attached a bomb; Spider-Man tricked him again making him to believe he was involved in the explosion of the door. As soon as the Murderer by Spider appeared from the resulting fog, Spidey attacked him and destroyed the device that controlled his Spider-Sense; he then left the unknown man to the police.

murderous lion.name: Murderous Lion
murderous lion.origin: Murderous Lion was one of the world's best fighters. A warlord who ruled over the Valley of Gates, which he had won by defeating his rivals. The Twelve Horrors were a group of martial arts masters in service to the Murderous Lion. In 1942, Murderous Lion was a member of "The Covenant," a group that has been around for many years that hoped to prevent universal threats to Earth and its people. Recently the Covenant was reconstituted, with the Murderous Lion as one of its members.

murdoch adams.name: Murdoch Adams
murdoch adams.origin: An American adventurer, Murdoch Adams was travelling across England when he stumbled across a demonic cult in York dedicated to the worship of the Celtic god Ludi, intent on sacrificing a young woman. Adams interrupted the ceremony, and was forced to confront Ludi himself. During the struggle, Adams accidentally struck a church bell, causing Ludi to recoil. Realising Ludi was vulnerable to loud noises and vibrations, Adams used the bell to drive him back to his own dimension. The Assyrian God Ningal sought revenge on Adams for the banishment of his ally, Ludi, and tormented Adams for many years. Eventually, Adams and Ningal would face each other; Ningal would kill Adams' lover, but Adams would succeed in trapping them both in an other-dimensional block of energy. There they both remained until they were both freed by the Dweller-in-Darkness. Adams re-materialised in Greenwich Village. Confused and disoriented, Adams sought out Dr Stephen Strange for help. Together with Strange, he travelled back to England to investigate Ningal's cult. En route, their plane came under attack from Ningal, though Strange was able to fight him off. Upon landing, Adams reconnected with his fiancee, Marcia Trent. Unknown to him, Trent was a cultist of Ningal, and she drugged him and tried to kill him. Before he passed out completely, he was able to use the power of a magical talisman Strange had given him for protection against Ningal and his followers. Adams survived the attack, but Trent died as a result.

murdock wwii.name: Murdock (WWII)
murdock wwii.origin: thumb|left|Murdock unmasked The man known only as Murdock was born to a wealthy family that owned the entire Cardiff Moor region near Camp Lehigh. One of the family's prized possession was the family pet, a massive hound dog. As the years progressed, the family was hit financial difficulties, and after hitting rock bottom, they were forced to give up their estate. Furious, Murdock's father vowed that his hound would destroy any who would come to live in Cardiff Moor. Many years later, Murdock -- now an old man -- returned to Cardiff Moor in 1941. By this time, the land was split up into a number of properties. Posing as a kindly old man, Murdock plotted to make his father's curse become true. Murdock painted his own hound with luminescent paint and sent it out to attack people. Dawning a hound inspired costume, Murdock confront his dog's victims and slew them. These series of murders led the people of Cardiff Moor to believe that the curse had come true. However, when a survivor of one of the "Phantom Hound's" attacks stumbled upon Camp Lehigh looking for help, it piqued the interest of Captain America and Bucky. thumb|The "Phantom Hound" of Cardiff Moor The two heroes visited Cardiff Moor and called on Murdock as he was visiting with his neighbor Mary Scott. He told Captain America and Bucky the legend of the Moor (omitting his personal relation to the family) before introducing him to the neighbors who were all frightened of the "phantom" and were ready to leave the area. Murdock spotted Captain America noticing a dog bone left out from his pet, prompting him to douse the lights and leave a note from the "hound", warning those who stayed in the Moors would be killed. Undeterred by this, Captain America and Bucky went out looking for the hound. The neighbors were inspired to look for the "hound" as well, and Murdock joined them. Murdock then broke away from the others, and in a cave where he hid his supplies, he put on his costume and released his vicious hound to hunt down and kill everyone looking for him. The hound and Murdock murdered a writer named Ramon before Captain America and Bucky could come to his rescue. Unleashing his hound on Mary Scott, Murdock's ruse was further realized when Captain America slew the dog and learned that it was not a phantom at all. Murdock then confronted Captain America, and in a one-on-one fight, Murdock was knocked out cold and unmasked. Putting the pieces of the puzzled together, Captain America realized that Murdock was related to the family who used to own the Moors, and he would be left to the authorities. Murdock's fate is unknown.

murgor tsoggua.name: Murgor-Tsoggua
murgor tsoggua.origin: ===Origin and early years=== Murgor-Tsoggua was a demon and dark god served by amphibian-like humanoid monsters. He inhabited a plane in the vast space between the stars. Ages before the Hyborian Age of Conan, Murgor-Tsoggua was summoned and bound in servitude by an ancient sorcerer. According to legends, Murgor-Tsoggua and his servants terrorized Tarantia, the capital city of Aquilonia, for decades, the latter providing souls to keep Murgor-Tsoggua alive, who in turn provided services to the sorcerer for his own means. Eventually, it all stopped, presumably with the sorcerer's death. The philosopher Alcemides, who had learned much on the matter from legends, theorized that Murgor-Tsoggua lied dormant, waiting for a mage to summon him from the other plane. Murgor-Tsoggua's servants persisted, in the tombs under Tarantia unsuspected, feeding on the dead of the city. ===Hyborian Age=== As part of a greater plan devised by the sorcerers Jumbassa, Urazai, and Scyllanato to defeat Conan, to avenge himself, Mimus had prepared a vision of himself to appear to his daughter Darweena and make her go in a tomb to preside over a sacrificial ceremony aiming to strengthen Murgor-Tsoggua, a tavernkeeper, the guard Bellus, and Conan's son Conn, all captured by Murgor-Tsoggua's servants. With each sacrifice, Murgor-Tsoggua grew stronger, and could complete his entry to the Earth plane with the third and final life. Conn managed to escape, and when Conan and Alcemides finally arrived to the crypt, the guard accompanying them was used azsc the third life, and the door opened, Murgor-Tsoggua attempting to cross the threshold, but was stopped by them. Alcemides then sealed the mystic portal and urged Conan to seal the catacombs as well. As Alcemides started the sealing of the catacombs, Conan rushed into the catacombs with a silver sword he had made to be forged to confront the demon, and found his son. By the time they exited the catacombs, Murgor-Tsoggua's servants infiltrated the palace and completed the ceremony, allowing Murgor-Tsoggua to pass the threshold in order to enact Mimus' vengeance. Murgor-Tsoggua neutralized Zenobia and Conn, and killed Darweena, but as he had feasted on three souls already, could not digest Darweena's. In a mist form, she managed to distract Murgor-Tsoggua, allowing Conan to strike and repel it through the gate. As Darweena was the sorcerer who had summoned it back and that she was herself stuck in the dark god's plane, Conan theorized that Murgor-Tsoggua was banished from the Earth plane.

murius.name: Murius
murius.origin: Murius was a Kree scientist and wife of Falzon, both specializing in photometric research. Shortly after their son Arides was born, he was selected by the Kree Supreme Intelligence to be used in the Personal Service Corps. Despite the protests of his parents, he was taken from them by force in order to process him for this service. Since Falzon and Murius were both experts in the conversion of light into energy they were given a new project to develop super-powered Kree soldiers using these photometric sciences. To their shock, they were reunited with their infant son, Arides, as he was to be their experimental prototype. His parents were unable to refuse experimenting on their son as he would have been killed right there in front of them had they chosen not to participate. Every day, for the first twenty years of his life, Arides was placed into a chamber where his parents focused concentrated photometric energies onto his growing body. At full maturity he was given a power suit attuned to his powers and he was given the code name Shatterstar. The Kree overseers approved of the outcome of the experimental treatments, though Murius and Falzon were disgusted at what they had turned their son into. Murius pleaded to her husband to take all three of them away from the Kree Homeworld and escape to Malador, a rustic planet where they could disappear and start over. She wanted a chance to give her son the nurturing he was denied for so long so that he would be more than just a killing machine for the Kree. Arides overheard his mother and father discussing their escape plan and instantly lashed out against them, condemning them as traitors. Though Arides had made quite clear his disgust for them both, his parents still loved their son too much to leave for Malador without him. Arides informed the overseers of his parents' plans to escape and, as Shatterstar, was placed in charge of their arrest. Only after his parents had learned of this betrayal to Kree command did they decided to try and escape on their own but it was too late. Shatterstar caught up with them at their spaceship before they could leave. Falzon surrendered immediately but Murius tried to run. Shatterstar shot his mother dead on the spot and then arrested his father who was put into a psychological rehabilitation program to reintroduce loyalty to the Kree Empire.

murna jessup.name: Murna Jessup
murna jessup.origin: Harvey Jessup, a scientist from Central City, California, was colleagues with Reed Richards. While Richards went on to become the leader of the super-heroes known as the Fantastic Four, Jessup began using his expertise in nuclear energy to work for the Republic Oil and Gas Company (later known as Roxxon). When Jessup's manager pressured him to cut corners in the building of a nuclear reactor, Jessup refused and was then fired. With nuclear disarmament talks between the United States of America and Russia were not making any progress, Jessup became afraid that the world was going to be destroyed in a nuclear war. Harvey was later inspired when watching a new interview with the Fantastic Four, wherein Reed Richards expressed an interest in field-effect phenomena. This inspired Harvey to use F.E.P. to protect his people from nuclear attack. For the next six years, Harvey Jessup worked on a device he would later call the Salvation Machine. The intention was that the device would place a protective dome around Central City where time inside the dome would move slower than outside, eventually the dome would be dropped once it was safe to venture outside. When Jessup's invention was complete, he activated the device, surrounding Central City with a massive black dome that kept it separated from the outside world. Either by accident or design, the Salvation Device did the opposite it intended: It sped up time within the dome, so much so that for every second that went by outside an entire month passed within. With fifty loyal technicians, Jessup rounded up the people of Central City and placed them in a state of suspended animation. Taking on the role of Great Coordinator, Jessup began advancing his society. Jessup maintained a centuries old life thanks to being placed in suspended animation, only being taken out when absolutely necessary. His followers formed a religion based on the Fantastic Four. They then began building up the city into a massive utopia. However, Harvey began to suspect something was wrong, but would not consider lowering the dome for fear that his theory of nuclear Armageddon proved to be true. Hundreds of years passed within the dome and it was eventually breached by the Avenger known as Iron Man, who remained within Central City, hunted by Jessup's minions for three weeks before escaping back outside. At some point, Jessup had a daughter, Murna, was born and it was discovered that she had mental powers, so Harvey set her up as a priestess. Following the Iron Man incident, Jessup created an army to defend his utopia, and engineered later generations into protectors of the realm: the Clobber Patrol, the Fire Patrol, the Wing Patrol, and Mind Patrol. The patrols were based upon the Thing, Human Torch, Mister Fantastic, and the Invisible Woman respectively. Hundreds more years passed and the dome was breached by the She-Hulk, who had recently replaced the Thing as a member of the Fantastic Four at the time. Jessup had his minions subdue her, but his daughter Murna protested, realizing that there was something not right about her father's plan. In response, Jessup had Murna exiled and the She-Hulk placed in suspended animation. After centuries had passed within the dome, the Fantastic Four and their ally Wyatt Wingfoot ended up breaching the dome to find their missing comrade, and discovered the civilization Jessup created within. After battling with the various patrols, the Fantastic Four were greeted by Princess Livia puppet ruler of the people. They were brought to the Grand Controller, who Richards had figured out was his old colleague. At first believing that they were impostors, Jessup decided to try and destroy the Fantastic Four instead of losing his position as a savior. The Invisible Woman was able to protect them with their invisibility powers and they were soon assisted in escaping by Murna. Murna in turn helped the Fantastic Four confront her father and free She-Hulk. During the ensuing battle against the Grand Coordinator, Murna was able to mind link Harvey with Reed Richards and force him to see the truth. Realizing the errors of his ways, Jessup agreed to let the people of Central City go free from suspended animation and go their own way with the Fantastic Four. Harvey died soon after, and the Fantastic Four freed Jessup's prisoners. Reed then used the Salvation Machine to send the future world of Central City deep into the future where it hopefully could thrive in peace.

murray anderson.name: Murray Anderson
murray anderson.origin: Dr. Murray Anderson was a scientist and the Director of U.S. Army's Project Rebirth. While General Phillips and Under-Secretary Homer Simms were talking to President Roosevelt, Anderson arrived at the White House and interrupted them, informing the officers that Project Rebirth was going to be executed. Anderson then led Phillips and Simms to Project Rebirth Curios Shop Facility, where Rebirth's candidate, Steve Rogers, was going to be enhanced by Dr. Abraham Erskine's Super-Soldier Serum. Anderson was between the group of people watching the experiment, while Nazi spy Heinz Kruger, disguised as Special Agent Fred Clemson, shot Erskine dead, and was subsequently killed by Rogers. He later helped forming the supergroup known as the Invaders. Many years later, he worked at the burn ward at the South Queens Hospital for Sick Children and was Janet Darling's superior. He complimented her for Thomas H. Hanson's case report, he found it very thorough and was amazed by the wealth of detail.

muse.name: Muse
muse.origin: Muse was a mysterious, deranged artist whose gruesome work of art was discovered after he anonymously sent the vigilante Blindspot the address of the warehouse in Washington Heights where he had planted it. This work consisted of a mural painted with blood from over a hundred different missing people. Some weeks later, he defaced the mural, and replaced most of it with the phrase, "You're only as good as your last performance" followed by a new address that directed the police to a vacant building. Inside one of the floors, Muse had planted the corpses of six Inhumans he had previously abducted, posing them with props as if they were performing mundane tasks. thumb|left|Muse is confronted by Daredevil A.D.A. Matt Murdock, who was one of the people that discovered Muse's second artwork, sensed Muse's presence in the distance, witnessing as people unveiled his new work for the first time, and left the scene to change into his Daredevil suit and confront the villain. However, Muse drove him off using a dummy grenade, and made his escape. During his first public appearance, Muse attacked a courtroom and kidnapped Judge Laird, who had been presented by Councilwoman Andrea Pearson with the case to shut down public access to the location of his blood mural. Muse took the judge to the sewers, where he had also abducted Pearson and two police officers, and planned to use all of them for a new work. Blindspot, who had witnessed the judge's kidnapping, followed Muse and caught his attention. Muse chased Blindspot deeper into the sewers, but the vigilante used his suit's camouflaging to disconcert Muse and return to the victims to tie them off and escort them to safety. Blindspot tried to lead Muse away again, but his suit ran out of batteries, and Muse captured him. Muse took Blindspot to his garret and while he was deciding what to do with him, Daredevil arrived, having tracked them down with his senses. Muse gouged Blindspot's eyes out and then escaped. On his way out, he passed by a room where all of the missing people used in his mural were hanging from the ceiling being drained of their blood, and still alive. He cut the ropes hanging them to distract Daredevil and save time, but he was stopped on the rooftop by Inhuman authorities, who had been assisting Daredevil in investigating Muse due to the crimes on Inhumans. thumb|right|220px|Muse's face revealed Daredevil caught up with him once Muse had been cuffed, fueled by rage for Blindspot's injury. Having noticed Daredevil's intentions, Muse broke his own fingers, stating that's what Daredevil would've wanted, for him to be unable to create more works of "art." After Daredevil took off Muse's mask, the villain was taken away. Muse was subsequently imprisoned at the high-security detention level of New Attilan. His hands healed eventually. Following the election of Wilson Fisk as Mayor of New York City and his implementation of strict anti-vigilante policies, Muse became inspired by Daredevil's continued fight for justice in spite of the persecution, and decided to escape, killing twelve guards in the process. He went on to vandalize numerous landmarks of Manhattan with giant-sized irremovable graffiti that featured different vigilantes showing support for them. A group of police officers intercepted Muse when he was finishing a mural of the Punisher. Muse slaughtered them and adorned the graffiti with their bodies. Mayor Fisk used the tragedy to push his anti-vigilantism agenda, by blaming the Punisher for it. Having regained his sight due to the intervention of The Hand, Blindspot decided to confront Muse on his own. He defaced one of Muse's murals to lure the murderous artist, and they fought. When Muse overpowered Blindspot, he was briefly taken over by the power of The Hand's Beast, and defeated Muse. However, he refused to kill him. In response, Muse walked into a burning pile of debris complaining that it was supposed to be his own story and not Blindspot's. He succumbed to the fire, using his final words to lament because he had "so much beauty left." Following his death, Muse was condemned to eternity in Hell where he quickly grew accustomed to. He continued making art out of the suffering around him, but still wished to spread his word on Earth. One day, he witnessed the arrival of Morgan Whittier's soul, a struggling young artist who felt like losing her mind. Recognizing her as a kindred spirit, Muse went to her and shared his view of the world with Morgan, inspiring her to continue his legacy when she returned to the land of the living. Although at first Morgan thought this was all an hallucinatory dream, Muse began appearing to her as a ghost to drive her to unleash her true self. She killed her art teacher and began making macabre artworks out of her victims, all the while under the supervision of Muse, though their activities caught the attention of the second Daredevil. Muse and his pupil created an evil doppelganger of Daredevil named Helektra wh

musenda.name: Musenda
musenda.origin: Musenda taught Blade how to hunt vampires along with Orji, Azu, and Ogun. The group managed to capture and stake Dracula, but he was revived by Kuai Hua and waited for the group to return, killing two of them. A third died a while later, leaving only Musenda and Blade alive. Blade took his boots and used them as part of his second costume.

musere.name: Musere
musere.origin: Musere was among the soldiers at Karere, sent there because of the Warpies bloom. When Beast, Storm and Wolverine goes into the woods to look after a form seen and shot on by the soldiers, Doctor Crocodile decided to let Musere and his fellow soldier Nagenda go with them, to the disappointment of Cyclops. When the stranger, an alternate Jim Jaspers was finally found, one of the two soldiers ask him to freeze and immediately shot him. The two of them were taken down by a Storm's burst, and threatened by Wolverine. It is unknown if they survived to the following battle against the Furies.

After learning that Alchemax was going to sell a fleet of Spider-Slayers to Trans-Sabal's ruler, she had one of the sellers kidnapped. She initially tried to force him to cancel the sale, but she then tried to convince him to use the spider-slayers to overthrow Dahn instead. When the Scorpion and Spider-Man attempted to rescue Stone, they began to fight each other. Their battle caused the building they were in to collapse, and Mussaret gave her life to save Ty. Inspired by her sacrifice, he used the slayers to force Dahn out of the country.

mustang.name: Mustang
mustang.origin: Mustang was a former U.S. Navy pilot and stunt flyer who lived in a trailer park in the New Mexico desert after suffering severe injuries in an aircraft crash. The accident left him blind and dependent on extensive prosthetics and medical equipment, including a dialysis shunt and artificial joints. He subsequently became a patient of Doctor Prospero, hoping the doctor's treatments would restore his sight. Mustang encountered the fugitive X-Men while they were crossing the desert and offered them food and shelter. Despite being unable to see, his heightened awareness and experience as a pilot allowed him to recognize that they were mutants on the run. After Wolverine investigated Prospero's clinic, Jean Grey transferred his memories into Mustang's mind, allowing him to witness the clinic's horrifying secret: Prospero was transforming his patients into Prime Sentinels. Realizing that his hoped-for treatment would cost him his humanity, Mustang helped the X-Men evade Bastion's forces by hiding them in an underground compartment beneath the trailer camp. He subsequently attempted to warn the other patients about what was happening at the clinic. Mustang and the other patients of the Prospero Clinic were transformed into Prime Sentinels when their cybernetic implants were activated in the presence of the X-Men. Horrified by what had happened to his friends, Mustang rejected the possibility of undergoing the same transformation, despite the prospect of regaining his sight and fully recovering from his injuries. After the X-Men defeated the three activated Prime Sentinels and decided to destroy the clinic, Mustang and the other residents of the trailer park helped them raid the facility. The clinic was eventually destroyed, with its staff apparently abandoning the premises. However, Bastion subsequently ordered the activation of a specially equipped sleeper Prime Sentinel that had been implanted in Mustang. While the X-Men searched the ruined clinic, Mustang suddenly began to convulse as his body underwent a cybernetic transformation. His damaged eyes were restored, allowing him to see with remarkable clarity, but the process simultaneously overwhelmed his personality with the Sentinel's programming. Mustang was transformed into a Prime Sentinel and, under Bastion's remote directive, identified the X-Men as mutant designates and prepared to terminate them. Following the destruction of the Prospero Clinic, Mustang was remotely activated as a sleeper Prime Sentinel. His body transformed into a cybernetic hunter-killer, and he immediately identified Wolverine, Cyclops, and Cannonball as mutant designates. Wolverine attempted to reach the man beneath the programming, reminding Mustang of how he had once remained aboard his crippled aircraft rather than allow it to crash into a crowd of civilians. For a moment, Mustang appeared to resist the Prime Directive, but the programming ultimately compelled him to attack. While Cyclops and Cannonball evacuated the remaining patients, Wolverine stayed behind to confront Mustang. He appealed to Mustang's humanity by comparing his own experience of being transformed into a living weapon with what Bastion had done to him. Mustang nevertheless continued attacking, claiming that mutants posed a threat to humanity and that he had to follow his Prime Directive. Jubilee eventually entered the fight and struck Mustang in the eyes with her pyrotechnic powers, overloading his visual receptors. The attack caused him to regain his sight only momentarily before the damage forced him to wonder what he had done. Although the Prime Directive remained active, Mustang was no longer completely under its control. After the X-Men escaped the clinic, Wolverine gave Mustang the computer disks containing the records of the patients converted into Prime Sentinels. He explained that the information could help locate the other sleeper units and potentially reverse their transformations. Mustang admitted that it would be difficult to remain in control for long and warned Wolverine that he might eventually be unable to resist the programming and be forced to hunt him down. Wolverine advised him to give the disks to S.H.I.E.L.D., whose technicians might be able to suppress the Prime Directive and find a way to restore him. Mustang agreed and remained behind as the X-Men departed with the wounded Cyclops. Despite having regained enough of his humanity to resist Bastion's programming, Mustang was once again blind and still faced the possibility of becoming a Prime Sentinel against his will.

mutant baboon.name: Mutant Baboon
mutant baboon.origin: In his illicit experimentation on mutant genomes and genetic deviation, the mad scientist and former Genoshan experimentation division advocate Dr. Paine experimented on some of the local wildlife in Niganda, Africa. One of those Experiments begat a super intelligent baboon whom served him begrudgingly, as the bad doctor regularly abused him for his failures. In retaliation he secretly worked on a virus that would kill mankind while leaving simians like himself unharmed, while eventually convincing two of the Red Ghost's super apes to join him in his genocidal vengeance. They were all stopped by the untimely arrival of Black Panther, Storm, and the rest of the X-Men moments after he'd tossed the virus off the roof. ===New Management=== Eventually he ended up back in the services of the humans he hated so much for creating him. This time he acted as the technical specialist to N'Jadaka who served as the puppet monarch of the U.S. while he staged a takeover of Wakanda by commandeering its rival nation of Niganda. Through his help, N'Jadaka was able to appear as a hero and leader through the Baboon's machinations, which he'd used to force-evolve other animals into a private militia/present threat that he could use to project his idol worship. This even involved developing specialized technology that enabled both him and N'Jadaka to entrap and utilize the unique constitution of Spectrum for their own personal gain when the latter was sent to rein him in. As a contingent of Wakandan soldiers led by Zuri had come to the source of the force field technology which bound and trapped Monica, the Baboon boasted of his Force Field Device, which shielded him, Niganda and whomever else he chose while also returning fire through the same tech apparatus that siphoned off Spectrum's energy. When the former managed to free herself from her confinement, he seemingly disappeared into thin air before anyone could detain him.

mutant master.name: Mutant Master
mutant master.origin: An alien who plotted to conquer Earth used a costume to make himself appear human. Thus, he crafted the identity of the Mutant-Master, a mutant seeking to conquer humanity so that mutantkind could rule. thumb|left|Mutant Master's true form The Mutant-Master planned to cause an explosion within a high-level Russian meeting, knowing that the United States would be blamed. The workers at an American missile base would be gassed, and his agents would launch their nuclear weapons at Russia, leading to World War Three and the destruction of the human race. In the carnage that remained, with these two major world powers destroyed, a third group, Factor Three, would seize power. The Mutant-Master learned of a mutant metamorph and followed his trial to the house of Jack Bolton, which was occupied by the mutant metamorph who had taken Bolton's form. Using a report on Bolivar Trask's Sentinels, the Mutant-Master convinced the metamorph that humanity saw mutants as a threat and would try to destroy them, and that mutantkind should rule the world. Naming the metamorph the "Changeling," the Mutant-Master convinced him to accept the role of his second-in-command in Factor Three, where he would handle his day-to-day operations. The Changeling then recruited the Blob, Mastermind, Unus, and the Vanisher from among the X-Men's greatest enemies to serve as their fighting force, as well as the operative Ogre. Using the Mutant-Master's technology, the Changeling implanted a bomb within the mutant Banshee's headband, forcing him to serve Factor Three under the threat of death. The Mutant-Master sent the Ogre and the Vanisher to ambush Humus Sapien, placing a control helmet on him to inhibit his power. He then sent the Ogre and Banshee to abduct Professor X, who detected the mutant members of Factor Three (see comments). The Ogre located the secret headquarters of the X-Men. Though the Ogre nearly succeeded in their first attempt, both Banshee and Ogre were captured by the X-Men, and the Banshee revealed how he had been forced to serve Factor Three via the explosives in his headband. Professor X mentally disabled the explosives, allowing the removal of the headband and freeing Banshee from Factor Three's servitude. The Banshee told them that Factor Three was the most dangerous secret organization on the Earth, and that they had the means to conquer the world or even to destroy it. After escaping, the Ogre returned to Factor Three, only to be chastised by the Mutant-Master for his failure, and instructed to wait at Factor Three's base until the Mutant-Master could return to deal with him further. Meanwhile, the Banshee started a weeks-long search of the mountains and valleys of Central Europe for the base of Factor Three. He was aided by advanced detection equipment given to him by Professor X. Professor X locked himself in a room and shut off his thoughts to the outside world while he focused on researching Factor Three, but was pulled from his research by the Warlock (later Merlin Demonspawn). After the Warlock was defeated, Professor X reminded the X-Men of the threat of Factor Three. Before long, Cerebro failed to detect any more emissaries of Factor Three in the USA. Telling the X-Men about Cerebro's findings (or lack thereof), Professor X gave them the weekend off. After they departed, he resumed his vital experiments, pausing only to notify the other X-Men after receiving a mental message from Cyclops. Completing his experiments, Professor X attempted to restore the Juggernaut, whom he had rendered inert in their last battle. Professor X began to use his Energo-Transformer to drain the Juggernaut's power so he could then cure his embittered mind. However, as he did so, he sensed a new, powerful alien force entering the Juggernaut's mind, adding to his own natural resistance. As a result, the device was destroyed, and the Juggernaut instead gained Professor X's telepathic powers, rendering X unconscious. The Juggernaut subsequently overpowered the X-Men, but as he prepared to destroy their school and bury them under it, he was telepathically contacted by Factor Three. They revealed that they had caused the explosion which freed the Juggernaut and instructed him to leave the X-Men behind, steal a jet to Europe, and join them. Though irritated at being commanded, the Juggernaut nonetheless decided to follow their instructions. He wished to add their power to his so that they could conquer the world. As the Juggernaut continued on his mission to steal a ship to travel to Factor Three's European base, Cyclops and Marvel Girl, learning of Xorak the Outcast - a resident of the Crimson Cosmos accessed via the Crimson Ruby of Cyttorak - used a mystic spell to access the Ruby and defeat Xorak, pulling the Juggernaut within the Ruby as well. However, while the X-Men were battling the Juggernaut, android agents of Factor Three entered the X-Mansion and kidnapped Professor X. The androids wrecked Cerebro as well before departing the X-Ma

Thus, he crafted the identity of the Mutant-Master, a mutant seeking to conquer humanity so that mutantkind could rule. thumb|left|Mutant Master's true form The Mutant-Master planned to cause an explosion within a high-level Russian meeting, knowing that the United States would be blamed. The workers at an American missile base would be gassed, and his agents would launch their nuclear weapons at Russia, leading to World War Three and the destruction of the human race. In the carnage that remained, with these two major world powers destroyed, a third group, Factor Three, would seize power. The Mutant-Master learned of a mutant metamorph and followed his trial to the house of Jack Bolton, which was occupied by the mutant metamorph who had taken Bolton's form. Using a report on Bolivar Trask's Sentinels, the Mutant-Master convinced the metamorph that humanity saw mutants as a threat and would try to destroy them, and that mutantkind should rule the world. Naming the metamorph the "Changeling," the Mutant-Master convinced him to accept the role of his second-in-command in Factor Three, where he would handle his day-to-day operations. The Changeling then recruited the Blob, Mastermind, Unus, and the Vanisher from among the X-Men's greatest enemies to serve as their fighting force, as well as the operative Ogre. Using the Mutant-Master's technology, the Changeling implanted a bomb within the mutant Banshee's headband, forcing him to serve Factor Three under the threat of death. The Mutant-Master sent the Ogre and the Vanisher to ambush Humus Sapien, placing a control helmet on him to inhibit his power. He then sent the Ogre and Banshee to abduct Professor X, who detected the mutant members of Factor Three (see comments). The Ogre located the secret headquarters of the X-Men. Though the Ogre nearly succeeded in their first attempt, both Banshee and Ogre were captured by the X-Men, and the Banshee revealed how he had been forced to serve Factor Three via the explosives in his headband. Professor X mentally disabled the explosives, allowing the removal of the headband and freeing Banshee from Factor Three's servitude. The Banshee told them that Factor Three was the most dangerous secret organization on the Earth, and that they had the means to conquer the world or even to destroy it. After escaping, the Ogre returned to Factor Three, only to be chastised by the Mutant-Master for his failure, and instructed to wait at Factor Three's base until the Mutant-Master could return to deal with him further. Meanwhile, the Banshee started a weeks-long search of the mountains and valleys of Central Europe for the base of Factor Three. He was aided by advanced detection equipment given to him by Professor X. Professor X locked himself in a room and shut off his thoughts to the outside world while he focused on researching Factor Three, but was pulled from his research by the Warlock (later Merlin Demonspawn). After the Warlock was defeated, Professor X reminded the X-Men of the threat of Factor Three. Before long, Cerebro failed to detect any more emissaries of Factor Three in the USA. Telling the X-Men about Cerebro's findings (or lack thereof), Professor X gave them the weekend off. After they departed, he resumed his vital experiments, pausing only to notify the other X-Men after receiving a mental message from Cyclops. Completing his experiments, Professor X attempted to restore the Juggernaut, whom he had rendered inert in their last battle. Professor X began to use his Energo-Transformer to drain the Juggernaut's power so he could then cure his embittered mind. However, as he did so, he sensed a new, powerful alien force entering the Juggernaut's mind, adding to his own natural resistance. As a result, the device was destroyed, and the Juggernaut instead gained Professor X's telepathic powers, rendering X unconscious. The Juggernaut subsequently overpowered the X-Men, but as he prepared to destroy their school and bury them under it, he was telepathically contacted by Factor Three. They revealed that they had caused the explosion which freed the Juggernaut and instructed him to leave the X-Men behind, steal a jet to Europe, and join them. Though irritated at being commanded, the Juggernaut nonetheless decided to follow their instructions. He wished to add their power to his so that they could conquer the world. As the Juggernaut continued on his mission to steal a ship to travel to Factor Three's European base, Cyclops and Marvel Girl, learning of Xorak the Outcast - a resident of the Crimson Cosmos accessed via the Crimson Ruby of Cyttorak - used a mystic spell to access the Ruby and defeat Xorak, pulling the Juggernaut within the Ruby as well. However, while the X-Men were battling the Juggernaut, android agents of Factor Three entered the X-Mansion and kidnapped Professor X. The androids wrecked Cerebro as well before departing the X-Ma
equipment: A robotic exoskeleton that made him appear human
fields.notes: While he posed as a human or humanoid, his true form was that of a cephalopod-like animal with ten tentacles. He spent most of his known appearances seated within a mobile platform. It enabled him to travel via directed hovering. It somewhat resembled Professor X's Hoverchair in transport mode. He used a force field to protect himself from attacks, but this seemed to be part of his technological abilities.

muthos.name: Muthos
muthos.origin: Muthos was the well-respected chief consular to Geirrodur, King of the Rock Trolls. When Geirrodur's ambitious chief warrior Ulik challenged Thor Odinson in an attempt to capture his enemy, Muthos adviced his King to not trust Ulik, something that the King found too obvious. Geirrodur's wife, Queen Ulla, when asked about the duel, gave her support to Ulik instead of Thor, and Muthos openly suggested that she was not saying all she was thinking. Geirrodur then dismissed Muthos, warning him of his treason-tantamount words. However, soon afterward, Muthos' word revealed to be precise, as Ulla suddenly sided with Thor in a key point of his duel and then usurped Geirrodur's throne. One of the few Trolls loyal to Geirrodur, Tyborr, warned his king against Ulla, remembering that Muthos, who had "never played the fool", had spoken against the queen.

muti xabbu sulaweyo.name: Muti (Xabbu Sulaweyo)
muti xabbu sulaweyo.origin: A mysterious Mutant hailing from the Mute Zones; working as a Vibranium miner while remaining off the grid. The unidentified Wakandan regularly bounced around his work space across the hidden African nation of Wakanda from time to time adopting new identities along the way. Muti would eventually make contact with Princess Shuri as her brother; King T'Challa was away exploring in outer space. Muti's hacking into her system mainframe using his abilities having piqued her interest with his audacity and ingenuity in accomplishing the deed. The two having become fast friends in the short span of two weeks time, the royal having enough faith in him to keep an eye out for her missing mother, Queen-Mother Ramonda, when asked too. While Shuri was at a meeting with the Egungun at the Birnin Zana Community Center, Muti would contact her again about a weird happenstance occurring in the Sahara Desert of Mali. While the princess was near Timbuktu with Iron Man dealing with a black hole, Muti offered aid by issuing an evacuation notice to city through various means. Either though hacking boomboxes, light bulbs, and even non-digital wrist watches he reached out to the locals, something that the Griots found quite perplexing. After having given congrats to being anointed as the new Black Panther in her brother's absence, Muti sets off a nation wide tech shutdown of Shuri's technological network with his moniker labeled on the deed. A ploy which was carefully elaborated to draw Shuri and Storm to his exact location at the Mena Ngai where he'd managed to capture their space bug, which in turn ended up taking him over when he tried to control it. Muti came clean about who he was and what his plan had been with the Lubber his pen pal had been chasing for weeks, revealing how he was a mutant who found out catching and holding their intended quarry was easier said than done. Muti would aid Shuri one more time as they transported to the Djalia for the final bout against the Lubber. Finding his abilities had become supercharged while in the Wakandan realm of remembrance, he would stave off the space monster's genesis creations while Shuri did battle with it. Eventually coming to terms with the alien, Shuri, Muti, and Mansa returned to the living world, after which the two really got to know each-other on a more personal level as friends and as citizens of the realm.

mutt.name: Mutt
mutt.origin: Mutt attended a meeting between Jimmy-6 and the Kingpin which was crashed by the vampiric Hunger. Low-level goons in the Fortunato crime family, Mutt and T-Bone were sent by Jimmy-6 to Cypress Hills Cemetery to retrieve a chest. They grabbed the chest and fought the vampire mobsters guarding it in a running battle that eventually took them to a convenience store. Once there, they were assisted by Spider-Man and Blade, but managed to lose both T-Bone and the chest to the vampire mobsters. Mutt, Spider-Man, and Blade followed the vampires to an abandoned Roxxon factory on Manhattan's Lower West Side, where they confronted Hunger. Mutt found T-Bone, who had become one of Hunger's vampiric thralls and tried to feed off Mutt. Mutt staked him instead, weakening Hunger, and fled.

muzzafar lambert.name: Muzzafar Lambert
muzzafar lambert.origin: Saracen was an international mercenary and master swordsman who styled himself after the Muslim warriors of the Crusades. A lethal operative with expertise in bladed weapons, firearms, and covert tactics, he built a reputation as a disciplined and relentless killer for hire. He first crossed paths with the Punisher while pursuing a mutual target connected to extremist political factions. Though the two briefly cooperated when circumstances aligned, their alliance dissolved almost immediately, and Saracen ultimately marked Frank Castle as his primary objective. Severely wounded during one of their early encounters, he later recovered and returned fully to mercenary work. Saracen subsequently entered the employ of criminal and political interests tied to organized crime, operating in Sicily where he targeted Castle and those connected to him. He later orchestrated an attack that resulted in the death of Esmerelda Giovanni, further deepening Castle’s vendetta against him. In retaliation, the Punisher assassinated Saracen’s employer while disguised as Saracen, leaving the mercenary internationally wanted. Amid rising tensions between Zukistan and Trafia, Saracen resurfaced under the alias Colonel Hawk, acting as a security specialist embedded in the conflict. There, he interrogated the captured Punisher before Castle escaped. Their rivalry culminated in multiple violent confrontations, including a brutal hand-to-hand battle interrupted by the arrival of Microchip. Saracen continued taking high-risk contracts across international theaters of conflict, including work for rogue military figures. Their feud reached its apparent conclusion at a clandestine gathering of assassins and terrorists, where the Punisher infiltrated the event posing as Saracen himself. When the two finally faced each other, the confrontation devolved into a savage sword duel that ended with Castle driving a blade through Saracen’s heart, seemingly killing him.

mx39147.name: MX39147
mx39147.origin: Delphine Courtney was actually a robot MX39147, a highly advanced creation of the Brand Corporation, a subsidiary of Roxxon Oil. She was assigned to Roxxon's executive vice-president Jerome Jaxon as his assistant, though Jaxon did not know Courtney was not human. Jaxon held a grudge against the Canadian superhero team Alpha Flight and its leader James MacDonald Hudson, and on Jaxon's behalf, Courtney recruited a team of Alpha Flight's former trainees as Omega Flight to oppose them. Jaxon lured Hudson to New York City, where he had Omega Flight make their move against him and his team. Meanwhile, Courtney kidnapped Hudson's wife Heather and held her hostage while Omega Flight fought Alpha Flight. When Heather fought back, she scratched Courtney's face and to her shock, revealed the robotic form underneath. Although Omega Flight were defeated, Courtney escaped. Courtney rebuilt herself into a male humanoid form and created a duplicate of Guardian's battlesuit. Wearing fake skin and hair that disguised her as James McDonald Hudson, Courtney convinced Heather and the rest of Alpha Flight that she was Hudson. As Hudson, Courtney set up a trap for Alpha Flight with the surviving members of Omega Flight at the West Edmonton Mall. When Courtney tried to release Smart Alec from Shaman's Medicine Pouch, she inadvertently released out-of-control mystical forces. Omega Flight were confronted by Alpha Flight's ally Madison Jeffries, who destroyed Courtney. Courtney's Guardian battlesuit was salvaged and later used by Heather Hudson as Vindicator.

mxxptrm.name: Mxxptrm
mxxptrm.origin: Mxxptrm was a Martian who lived on Earth-5106 a reality where space travel and exploration blossomed in the 1950s and where the planet Mars could sustain life. He was part of the VDBN tribe, a group of barbaric Martains who knew nothing but violence who would attack anyone in their way, and failing to find enemies to crush would fight among themselves. However, by the year 2000, with Mxxptrm as their leader, the VDBN were exiled from Mars and decided to travel to Earth to learn how to live in peace. They were greeted by Space Squadron leader Jet Dixon. While introductions were rough, Mxxptrm and his crew tried to follow the Earthman's peaceful example until Mxxptrm saw Jet out with his fianceé Dawn Revere and instantly became jealous. Mxxptrm savagely attacked Jet, but the Squadron leader easily bested Mxxptrm in battle. Mxxptrm was shocked when Jet spared his life and he fled the scene unsure how to deal with mercy. He eventually kidnapped Dawn, her father Chief Bennett Revere and the Galaxy council. However this was only to denounce his barbaric ways and show that he could live peacefully with others. With the crisis over, Jet and Bennett offered Mxxptrm to join the Space Squadron, and the Martian accepted, taking on the nickname "Max". Max was also involved in investigating what force was causing the Mercurians to give into their evil personas. Taking the Space Squadron to Mercury they learned that the Sun had moved closer to Mercury increasing the temperature and causing the transformation in the Mercurians and stopping the Octopus-Men's attack on Neptune's Fish-Men. He later participated in the 2000 Olympics on the moon, stopping the intergalactic criminal named Boz and joined his team mates in an experiment to test Dr. Kalandra's gas that theoretically could make one immune to pain, hunger and the elements. While the gas worked it also had the side effect of causing painful, disorientating and random teleportations. However this proved fortuitous when they all teleported to Crag Mountain where they caught Edgar Revere about to sell Atomic Dust to a renegade band of Frogmen, stopping the transaction before it could be completed.

mygdalla.name: Mygdalla
mygdalla.origin: Mygdalla was one of the many aliens imprisoned in Impericon who were used as a leverage to make the person they meant the most for fight the Queen of Nevers, and was held captive even after said person had died in battle. When Dawn Greenwood was teleported to Impericon as the leverage to make the Silver Surfer fight the Queen, she made a plan of escape with which the prisoners broke free. Mygdalla managed to deduce where the fueling stations for escaping vehicled were, and the prisoners headed there. After Mygdalla and the other prisoners escaped Impericon while the Silver Surfer and Dawn confronted Zed in order to give the Queen of Nevers her heart back, they realized they could honor their loved ones by helping Dawn get the heart to the Queen. The prisoners fought the Gatekeepers and allowed Dawn to get the Queen's heart back to its rightful owner.

myla.name: Myla
myla.origin: Moondancer was a member of the Shi'ar Imperial Guard during the crisis that came to be known as Operation Galactic Storm. She was among a small strikeforce that battled Quasar in space, keeping the young Avenger busy long enough so that he could not interfere with the launch of the Nega-Bomb - the weapon that ended the war by killing 90% of the Kree population. Moondancer and her fellow Guardsmen Voyager and Solar Wind quit the Imperial Guard after they wished to help Quasar battle the enigmatic Stranger. The three Guardsmen had been captives of the Stranger for several years and wanted to take the opportunity to exact their revenge. After the Guard's leader, Gladiator, ordered the trio not to become involved they resigned from active duty.

myles alfred.name: Myles Alfred
myles alfred.origin: ===Early Life=== Myles Alfred was the son of Edward Alfred who was renowned in academic circles, but was neglectful and seldom present as a father. His mother was an ethnomusicologist by profession, and somewhat subservient at home. She was also described as an 'exponent of the North African 'ud'. thumb|left|200px Myles Alfred was an expert in literature and was known outside of his mutant fandom for his literary work. It was while studying at Harvard University that he authored a critically acclaimed piece on Walt Whitman. Myles' mutant powers were triggered when a group of college buddies harassed him. He left them with multiple slashes. At first, extreme emotions triggered his animal form but he learned to control it at will. thumb|Cover of ===X-Force=== When most of the original mutant team died during a hostage situation in a New York City music studio, Alfred joined the newly line-up of the media-drive mutant team X-Force. In their first outing and press conference, they were confronted by the old X-Force who wanted them to drop the name, as they were only using it for their own profit. A fight broke out, and Myles suffered broken glasses and an injured arm. Deciding to improve his public standing, he teamed with Phat in order to increase his status. This included jumping into a fight between Spike and Anarchist upon Spike's arrival on the team. They even faked a gay relationship for publicity. This backfired when they both realized they actually were gay. ===X-Statix=== Vivisector along with X-Statix, battled Bad Guy. He visited the movie set of the X-Statix movie and accompanied the male members of the team for a press conference. Myles suffered through the death of Phat, who sacrificed his life to save the rest of the team. He then went on to help Henrietta Hunter avenge her death. Her first death, that is, though she utilized the supernatural circumstances of her second death to do so. This involved the outright murder of a European head of state. This was enough to put Hunter to rest. ===Powerless=== He briefly lost his powers and left X-Statix after taking a serum to help him to return to a normal life. Dr. Alex Finlay, the doctor who "helped" Myles, used his method of stripping powers from mutants to give himself Myles' abilities. The procedure drove Dr. Finlay insane and implanted Myles' feelings of resentment toward his father into his mind. Myles was able to kill the deranged "Vivisector II" by using his father's birthday present from him--a solid gold ballpoint pen--to stab it in the eye. After that incident, Myles regained his powers and was able to rejoin X-Statix. Myles helps the team when Doop's brain becomes lost, parts of it in various spots on Earth. The team confronts the Avengers over Doop, as the Avengers know he is very dangerous. Myles loses his piece of the brain to Hawkeye, who lies to fool Myles into believing a partnership with the Avengers was possible. However, the team's willingness to do what they perceived was right convinces Captain America to hand over custody of Doop. ===Apparent Death=== After this mission, the team decided to retire. They held a going-away party, attended by multiple heroes, including the Avengers. While at the party, they were convinced to take one last final mission, clearing a billionaire's house of armed gunmen. Various circumstances led some of the team to believe this final mission was a set-up designed to kill X-Statix. The overwhelming odds killed the team one by one though they killed a large portion of their attackers. The gunmen wore the same uniforms as the hostage takers at the music studio so long ago. Myles was shot. ===Reforming X-Statix=== Myles survived being shot and the mission that killed almost all the rest of his teammates. He retired to focus on his writing only for, years later, Dead Girl and Doop to convince him to join the newly reformed X-Statix in order to confront Zeitgeist and his new team, The X-Cellent. He was eventually killed by Zeitgeist.

He visited the movie set of the X-Statix movie and accompanied the male members of the team for a press conference. Myles suffered through the death of Phat, who sacrificed his life to save the rest of the team. He then went on to help Henrietta Hunter avenge her death. Her first death, that is, though she utilized the supernatural circumstances of her second death to do so. This involved the outright murder of a European head of state. This was enough to put Hunter to rest. ===Powerless=== He briefly lost his powers and left X-Statix after taking a serum to help him to return to a normal life. Dr. Alex Finlay, the doctor who "helped" Myles, used his method of stripping powers from mutants to give himself Myles' abilities. The procedure drove Dr. Finlay insane and implanted Myles' feelings of resentment toward his father into his mind. Myles was able to kill the deranged "Vivisector II" by using his father's birthday present from him--a solid gold ballpoint pen--to stab it in the eye. After that incident, Myles regained his powers and was able to rejoin X-Statix. Myles helps the team when Doop's brain becomes lost, parts of it in various spots on Earth. The team confronts the Avengers over Doop, as the Avengers know he is very dangerous. Myles loses his piece of the brain to Hawkeye, who lies to fool Myles into believing a partnership with the Avengers was possible. However, the team's willingness to do what they perceived was right convinces Captain America to hand over custody of Doop. ===Apparent Death=== After this mission, the team decided to retire. They held a going-away party, attended by multiple heroes, including the Avengers. While at the party, they were convinced to take one last final mission, clearing a billionaire's house of armed gunmen. Various circumstances led some of the team to believe this final mission was a set-up designed to kill X-Statix. The overwhelming odds killed the team one by one though they killed a large portion of their attackers. The gunmen wore the same uniforms as the hostage takers at the music studio so long ago. Myles was shot. ===Reforming X-Statix=== Myles survived being shot and the mission that killed almost all the rest of his teammates. He retired to focus on his writing only for, years later, Dead Girl and Doop to convince him to join the newly reformed X-Statix in order to confront Zeitgeist and his new team, The X-Cellent. He was eventually killed by Zeitgeist.
abilities: Vivisector doesn't know how to swim. It is unknown if it depends on his mutant form, or on his capacities.
weaknesses: His power requires him to focus on his emotions, both negative and positive.

mynes.name: Mynes
mynes.origin: Mynes was the king of Lyrnessus, a city neighboring Troy, and was married to Briseïs. At the beginning of the Trojan War, Achilles and his Myrmidons ravaged the cities around Troy, including Lyrnessus. Mynes was killed by Achilles himself, and his widow Briseïs took as a slave for Achilles, then for Agamemnon.

myntril.name: Myntril
myntril.origin: Myntril is an alien creature who uses a Symbiote to act as an Agent of the Cosmos, a champion of the universe dedicated to protecting those in need, and he works together with Tarna. With the appearance of another Symbiote-wearing hero, the Earthling named Venom, Myntril and Tarna followed him for some time to see if he was worthy of being an Agent of the Cosmos. After one of Venom's missions, Venom's ship was abducted by Tarna's and Myntril's. Myntril stopped a fight between Venom and Tarna that sparked with the former's arrival, and briefed Venom on their job as Agents of the Cosmos. When the Venom symbiote succumbed to rage, Myntril oversaw its trial and bickered with Tarna, expressing the belief that it was fallen and beyond redemption. When Tarna betrayed the Agents of the Cosmos to help Flash, Myntril confronted her and Flash's team, engaging Hilla Rollo in combat. Commending her prowess, he nevertheless quickly subdued her using his symbiote. When Venom and Flash emerged from the trial, Myntril commended Tarna for standing alongside her friends, but reprimanded her that the Agents of the Cosmos need to be above such personal ties. He allowed her to accompany her newfound friends to help Flash, but warned that when she returned she would be placed on trial herself to determine if she was still worthy of being an Agent of the Cosmos.

myra haddock.name: Myra Haddock
myra haddock.origin: Dr. Myra Haddock served as the project director for the Prometheus Division of Department H. The Division worked on technologies that the Department had "appropriated" (stolen) from various sources. Her position allowed her to take part in the meetings of the Department leadership under Director X. However, she often avoided attending those meetings and she disliked the Department's bureaucracy. Puck once asked Myra out on a date. She did not decline, though she threatened to kill him if he entered a restricted area of her Division. He thought she was joking, but Myra was serious. Haddock once used the Prometheus Pit to hide Alpha Flight into the Microverse.

myra tangier.name: Myra Tangier
myra tangier.first_appearance: Kent Blake of the Secret Service Vol 1 13
myra tangier.origin: Myra Tangier was a spy who was known as the Snake who was active in the 1950s. She developed her own spy organization that consisted of spies, adventurers and Nazi war criminals, operating it out of Istanbul, Turkey. By 1953 her spy organization became of prime concern to the United States government. They pulled out their best Secret Service agent Kent Blake, who was at the time fighting in the Korean War to track down the Snake and shut down her spy organization. When Blake arrived, Myra pose as a cafe dancer while Blake met with his contacts. However, when one with information on her organization was killed, she lured Kent into a trap that saw him captured by her minions. Myra attempted to assassinate Kent herself, but the Secret Service agent broke free and tied her up, then called the authorities. When the police arrived to take the spies away, Myra had managed to break free from her bonds and escape. Since escaping she continued her spy activities and had later clashes with Kent Blake.

myraddin of ruta.name: Myraddin of Ruta
myraddin of ruta.origin: ===Origins and the Merlyn Gestalt=== ====The Merlyn Gestalt==== Much of Merlyn's early history is obscured by deliberate deception, contradictory legends, impostors and the sorcerer's own mastery of illusion. These accounts do not necessarily describe unrelated individuals. Merlyn exists as a physical gestalt formed from his counterparts across interconnected realities, allowing the resulting being to draw upon their collective knowledge, memories and abilities. Individual aspects can nevertheless manifest independently and occasionally influence the disposition of the whole. This unusual existence also explains why Merlyn can appear at different ages and experience events outside an ordinary linear sequence; the Watcher described him as living both backwards and sideways through time. ====Gwion Bach and Taliesin==== The earliest identifiable stage of Merlyn's life was preserved in the Welsh tale . He was originally a boy named Gwion Bach, a servant of the enchantress Cerridwen. After drinking the first drops of a potion intended to bestow wisdom upon Cerridwen's son, Gwion fled her by changing shape. Cerridwen eventually swallowed him and consequently became pregnant, later giving birth to him anew as the gifted bard Taliesin, who was subsequently identified with Merlyn. ====Early Life and Prophecies==== Traditions concerning Merlyn's youth described him as the son of a demon and Aldan, the daughter of King Conaan of Dyfed, as well as the twin brother of the prophetess Ganieda. After discovering that her seducer had been a demon in disguise, Aldan received a priest's blessing, drank holy water and took a vow of chastity, preventing her child from being born predisposed toward evil. The young Merlyn demonstrated magical talent at an early age, worshipped the Earth goddess Gaea and fashioned the horned giant Gargantua from whale bones. When King Vortigen attempted to build a stronghold in the Welsh mountains, his repeatedly collapsing foundations were blamed upon the absence of a sacrifice born without a human father. Merlyn was seized for that purpose but saved himself by revealing a subterranean pool beneath the construction site. Its disturbance released the imprisoned Welsh dragon Y Ddraig Goch, whose emergence Merlyn interpreted as a sign of the kingdom that would eventually unite Britain. He later advised Vortigen's successor Aurelius and helped transport a ring of stones from Ireland to England, creating Stonehenge. ====Apprenticeship under Necrom==== Only after these accounts of his youth did the already white-haired Merlyn study under Necrom alongside Feron on Earth-148. Necrom taught them about the enormous energy produced where dimensions intersected and brought both apprentices to Earth-616, where such an alignment was imminent. Feron summoned the Phoenix Force, whose power projected a tower at the same corresponding location throughout parallel realities, anchoring an interdimensional energy matrix. When Feron realized that Necrom intended to seize the Phoenix's power for himself, he turned against their master. While they fought, Merlyn entered the matrix and was swept through the Multiverse. Necrom escaped with a fragment of the Phoenix that he eventually transformed into the Anti-Phoenix, while Merlyn gradually learned to control the matrix. His immersion in energy connecting innumerable realities may have been the event that consolidated his counterparts into the Merlyn gestalt, although the exact cause of the amalgamation remains uncertain. ====Myraddin and Atlantis==== At a later point in Merlyn's non-linear personal history, he appeared during the prehistoric Atlantean era as Myraddin, a solar priest from the island of Ruta, near Avalon. When the destruction of Avalon was prophesied, Myraddin was entrusted with ancient writings and artifacts and accompanied the priestess Igraine and her daughter Morgan to safety before the island was consumed by a volcanic catastrophe. Adopting the name Merlin, he brought them to Britain, arranged for Igraine to marry Gorlois of Tintagel and later took Morgan to the Aran Islands as his student. ===Sorcerer Supreme and the Rise of Camelot=== ====Sorcerer Supreme==== Having brought Igraine and Morgan into Britain, Merlyn began arranging the circumstances that would produce the king he had foreseen. Around the beginning of the sixth century, he won a contest of magical ability that entitled him to become Earth's Sorcerer Supreme. Merlyn declined to formally accept the office, preferring to pursue his own designs, but effectively occupied the position for a brief period until a new sorcerer succeeded him. ====Uther and Arthur==== Merlyn subsequently advised Uther Pendragon. When Uther desired Gorlois' wife, Merlyn transformed him into Gorlois' likeness, enabling Uther to enter Tintagel and conceive a child with Igraine while the real Gorlois was killed in battle. In exchange for his assistance, Merlyn claimed the resulting son, Arthur, placed him in the care

myrina.name: Myrina
myrina.origin: Myrina was the queen of the Amazon nation over twenty thousand years ago, during the Pre-Cataclysmic Age. The decadent empire of Atlantis hired her and her Amazons to root out a nest of Gorgons in the Western Peaks of Atlantis. Myrina took many Gorgons as captive and integrated them into the Amazon nation. Myrina left Atlantis but left a garrison behind, which was slain by the Atlantean sorcerous rulers to avoid payment, thus earning the Amazons' hatred (that went on to this day) . Fearing the Amazons' wrath, they tried to harness a fraction of the power of the Axis Mundi into the Omphalos, causing the Great Cataclysm or rather furthering it.

myrn.origin: Myrn was a long-time friend of Zabyk, and was worked with him on his Hyper-Wave Bomb project. After completing his tasks, including situating his friend in an intricate exoskeletal suit of armor, Myrn was betrayed and fatally wounded. Just before he died, a band of Earth's heroes found him, and he warned Mr. Fantastic of the bomb before expiring. However, either due to a mistake on his part or perhaps a precaution against betrayal, the bomb only affected Skrulls, neutralizing their power of shape-shift for a time.

myrna woodson.name: Myrna Woodson
myrna woodson.origin: The Angel receives a letter from a lawyer informing him that he is one of the last surviving distant family members of the Harmon estate and that he is to come to Blackmoor, England. Arriving at Harmon Manor, he meets his other distant relatives Colonel Webber Woodson and his daughter Myrna, who are waiting another family member from Australia (Charles Harmon). Inside, Woodson tells the Angel that the property is apparently haunted ever since Duke Harmon died, and that there are jewels hidden somewhere in the house. Woodson leaves the Angel and Myrna alone to inspect the cellar. Down there, Woodson finds a coffin that suddenly springs open and he is accosted by what appears to be the ghost of Duke Harmon. Woodson's weak heart causes him to pass out. Later, Myrna begins to worry about her father, and they find him in the basement as he recovers. He tells them about his encounter with the "ghost" and the Angel checks the coffin and finds it empty. They then take Woodson to bed and they all retire for the night. In his room, the Angel is confronted by the ghost of Duke Harmon. Proving that the ghost is real, the Angel is told that he died a coward dying from a gunshot while fleeing from an enemy. He tells the Angel that once one of his descendant commits an act of bravery, he will finally be able to rest. The next morning, the Angel saves Myrna and Colonel Woodson from a falling chandelier. Then the organ starts playing, and the Angel finds that there is a second set of keys in a hidden room behind the organ. He is knocked out by a mystery assailant. He wakes up in a crypt, and the ghost reappears, telling the Angel that someone is impersonating him and helps the Angel find the secret passage out of the room. Examining the organ closer, they find an extra key and press it, revealing the hidden jewels from a hidden compartment in the organ. They are confronted by the fake ghost who reveals himself to be the missing relative from Australia who is trying to kill them all so that he can take all the jewels from himself. Suddenly another chandelier breaks loose and kills the man when it falls on him ending his threat. Because of the Angel's bravery, the real ghost tells him that he can now finally rest. The Angel then tells Myrna and the Colonel that they can keep his share of the fortune, as he does not need the money.

myron delasco.name: Myron Delasco
myron delasco.origin: Myron Delasco was a Hollywood actor active in the 1940s. By 1946 he had the lead role as the killer in a horror film titled "The Merry Widow Murderer," featuring a scissors-wielding killer who targeted widows and was compelled to stop his murderous sprees whenever the local clock tower chimed midnight. After the film was complete, Myron left Hollywood for his country retreat; however, caught on slick roads caused by a freak rainstorm, Deleasco had a car accident and suffered amnesia. Believing himself the Merry Widow Murderer, Delasco stalked back to the city to carry on his character's "revenge." Days later, his savage murder of a woman using a pair of scissors attracted the attention of Captain America and Bucky to the scene of the crime. Though Bucky tripped over the corpse, bumping into Captain America and allowing the killer to escape, Cap soon deduced the killer was imitating the movie and might be Delasco, who'd been reported missing. After Myron managed another successful killing, Captain America had Bucky pose as a woman, leading Delasco into a trap; when Cap tried to stop him, Delasco stabbed him with scissors and fled with Bucky as his prisoner, intent on slaying the boy on a nearby rooftop. However, Cap, scaling the nearby clock tower, pushed the clock ahead, causing it to toll midnight and Delasco to cease his attack. Cap attempted to snap Delasco out of his state of mind by yelling "cut", but Delasco -- either still insane, or realizing the horrors he had committed -- walked off the roof and fell to his death.

myron maclain.name: Myron MacLain
myron maclain.species: Human, Myron MacLain learned metallurgy in the 1930s
myron maclain.origin: Dr. MacLain began to develop super-strong metals for the US Government at the beginning of World War II. While experimenting on various alloys for use as tank armor in future battlefield, he accidentally created the ultra-resilient Vibranium-Steel alloy shield that is used by Captain America. MacLain worked for some time at the U.S. Department of Agriculture, secretly the cover for the Weapon X Program' activities after it's break with Weapon Plus; MacLain was approached by Department H agent Logan, who was in search for answers about his adamantium skeleton. After several decades of continued experiments, MacLain finally produced the formula for True Adamantium and gave it to the U.S. Government. When S.H.I.E.L.D. fell after the Skrull invasion, Dr. MacLain was listed as active at Hydra's Tarantula station. Whether this means MacLain was one of Hydra's agents undercover in S.H.I.E.L.D., was captured, or undercover on behalf of S.H.I.E.L.D. at Tarantula station is unknown.

He was recruited into the Avant Guard by the Painter who amplified their powers by binding their souls in a mystic ritual. During a show, he used his powers to attack his audience but was confronted by Spider-Man and the Human Torch. Eventually the pair found the lair of the Avant Guard and after a short battle and defeat, the Painter trapped Spark inside one of his paintings.

myrra dark dimension.name: Myrra (Dark Dimension)
myrra dark dimension.origin: Myrra was one of those who rebelled against Umar. She was also a member of the council who advised their leader, Clea. Myrra was part of a rebel council meeting at which it was agreed that the rebellion was at an impasse and needed more information on Umar's troop movements before they could plan effectively. When Clea stated that she would try again to probe the mind of their prisoner, Myrra pointed out that she hadn't had much luck in cracking Captain Orini's psychic shields and suggested that maybe she should let someone else try. Synth and Doctor Strange both agreed. Later, after Strange and Rahl revealed to Clea and the council that Umar was Clea's mother, Burhn immediately protested that it could not be that their leader was the daughter of the tyrant. Myrra called him a fool and pointed out that this revelation could be a rallying point for the rebellion since their commander's heritage was linked not only to Olnar the First but to the present usurper as well. This led to another council member suggesting that the people could be swayed to accepting Clea as regent, something that Clea immediately rejected, stating that she had agreed to lead the rebellion but not to rule the dimension.
